title: Sell Mineral Rights in Midvale, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Midvale, OH | Tuscarawas County
metaDescription: Midvale sits in Tuscarawas County's Utica flank. Learn how coal-country land history and split estates shape a mineral rights sale here.
heroLead: Midvale is a small community in Tuscarawas County, an area long associated with coal mining as much as oil and gas, which means mineral ownership here can involve more than one kind of subsurface right.
intro: Tuscarawas County's mineral history isn't only oil and gas. Coal mining shaped a lot of this region for generations, and it's not unusual for a single tract near Midvale to have separate historical severances for coal rights and for oil and gas rights, sometimes to different parties entirely. Sorting out which rights you actually own, and which you don't, matters before you talk to anyone about selling.

sections.heading: Coal rights versus oil and gas rights
paragraphs: If your deed mentions 'minerals' broadly, it's worth clarifying whether that historically included coal, which was often severed separately and earlier than oil and gas rights in this part of Ohio. A buyer interested in your oil and gas rights only needs to know that those specific rights are intact and in your name, regardless of what happened to any coal severance decades ago.

sections.heading: Tuscarawas County's position on the Utica flank
paragraphs: Tuscarawas sits on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, west of the thicker core in Carroll and Harrison counties. Activity here has been more selective, so value on a Midvale-area tract depends heavily on how close your specific parcel is to any recent permits or producing units.

sections.heading: Confirming your rights at the Tuscarawas County Recorder
paragraphs: The Tuscarawas County Recorder's office in New Philadelphia holds the severance, deed, and lease records for the Midvale area. Given the region's mixed coal and oil-and-gas history, it's worth being specific when you request records: ask for both mineral and oil-and-gas severance documents so nothing gets missed.

faqs.question: Were coal rights and oil and gas rights severed together in Tuscarawas County?
faqs.answer: Not always. It's common in this region for coal to have been severed separately, sometimes decades before or after oil and gas rights, so the two can have entirely different ownership chains on the same tract.

faqs.question: Is Midvale in an active part of the Utica play?
faqs.answer: Tuscarawas County generally sits on the flank, west of the thicker Carroll and Harrison county core. Activity is more selective here and depends on proximity to specific units and permits.

faqs.question: Where do I check what rights I actually own near Midvale?
faqs.answer: The Tuscarawas County Recorder's office in New Philadelphia keeps severance and deed records. Ask specifically for oil-and-gas mineral records, since coal severances in this county are sometimes recorded separately.
